extracted.intended_audience: Users of the SINGULAR computer algebra system (mathematicians / programmers) who use the multigrading.lib library for multigraded computations
extracted.subtask_description: Reference documentation for the procedures provided by the SINGULAR library multigrading.lib: usage, purpose, return values, notes and examples for multigrading / lattice / group / multidegree operations in SINGULAR.

rubrics_metrics.name: getLattice
rubrics_metrics.description: get associated grading group matrix, i.e. generators (cols) of the grading group
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Usage: getLattice([R[,opt]]). Return: intmat, the grading group matrix, or its hermite normal form if optional argument "hermiteNormalForm" is given or smith normal form if optional argument "smith" is given. Examples show getLattice() == L after setBaseMultigrading(M,L); print(getLattice("hermite")) to print the Hermite NF.

rubrics_metrics.name: createGroup
rubrics_metrics.description: create the group of the form (S+L)/L, i.e. S specifies generators, L specifies relations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Usage: createGroup(S, L); S and L are integer matrices. Return: group (a list representation). Examples: createGroup(S,L) then printGroup(G) to show Generators/Relations. Works for isomorphic multigradings and 'extreme case' examples in doc.

rubrics_metrics.name: createQuotientGroup
rubrics_metrics.description: create the group of the form (I+L)/L, where I is the square identity matrix of size nrows(L) x nrows(L).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Usage: createGroup(L) (shortcut). L specifies relations between free generators of Z^nrows(L). Return: group (representation of Z^n / L). Example: createQuotientGroup(L) and printGroup(G). Also shows equivalent general construction via createGroup(I,L).

rubrics_metrics.name: createTorsionFreeGroup
rubrics_metrics.description: create the free subgroup generated by S within the free Abelian group of rank nrows(S)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Usage: createTorsionFreeGroup(S); S is an integer matrix. Return: group. Example: createTorsionFreeGroup(S) is a shortcut; general way is createGroup(S,L) with L=0. Shows output of printGroup for torsion-free subgroup.

rubrics_metrics.name: printGroup
rubrics_metrics.description: prints the group G
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Usage: printGroup(G). G is a group (list) created by createGroup etc. Return: nothing. Example: printGroup outputs 'Generators:' and 'Relations:' lists for inspection.

rubrics_metrics.name: isGroup
rubrics_metrics.description: checks whether G is a valid group
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Usage: isGroup(G); G should be created by createGroup (or createQuotientGroup, createTorsionFreeGroup). Return: int, 1 if G is valid and 0 otherwise. Example: isGroup(createGroup(S,L)) returns 1.

rubrics_metrics.name: isGroupHomomorphism
rubrics_metrics.description: checks whether A defines a group homomorphism phi: L1 -> L2
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Usage: isGoupHomomorphism(L1,L2,A) (typo in header). L1 and L2 are groups, A is an integer matrix. Return: int, 1 if A defines the homomorphism and 0 otherwise. Examples show matrices A and B where A yields 1 and B yields 0 (not a homomorphism).

rubrics_metrics.name: isGradedRingHomomorphism
rubrics_metrics.description: test a multigraded group ring homomorphism defined by a ring map from R to the current ring, given by generators images f and a group homomorphism A between grading groups
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Usage: isGradedRingHomomorphism(R, f, A); R ring, f ideal (images of generators), A group homomorphism. Return: int, 1 for TRUE, 0 otherwise. Example: build rings with setBaseMultigrading, define map F and matrix A, then isGradedRingHomomorphism(r, ideal(F), A) returns 1 if compatible. Note: incompatible A returns 0 and createGradedRingHomomorphism should error.

rubrics_metrics.name: createGradedRingHomomorphism
rubrics_metrics.description: create a multigraded group ring homomorphism defined by a ring map from R to the current ring, given by generators images f and a group homomorphism A between grading groups
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Usage: createGradedRingHomomorphism(R, f, A). Return: graded ring homomorphism object. Example: after checking compatibility with isGradedRingHomomorphism, createGradedRingHomomorphism(r, ideal(F), A) returns a homomorphism which can be printed; incompatible inputs should raise an error.

rubrics_metrics.name: setModuleGrading
rubrics_metrics.description: attaches the multiweights of free module generators to 'm' (a module/vector)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Usage: setModuleGrading(m, G), m module/vector, G intmat. Purpose: attach multigrading weights to module generators. Warning: The method does not verify whether the multigrading makes the module/vector homogeneous; use isHomogeneous(m) to check. Examples: setBaseMultigrading(M,T); compute multiDeg(I) and attach to syzygy module S = setModuleGrading(S,V); getModuleGrading(S) == V; getGradedGenerator and multiDeg usage shown.

rubrics_metrics.name: getModuleGrading
rubrics_metrics.description: return integer matrix of the multiweights of free module generators attached to 'm'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Usage: getModuleGrading(m), where m is module/vector previously set with setModuleGrading. Return: intmat of multiweights. Examples demonstrate setting base multigrading, computing multiDeg(I), setting module grading and verifying equality with getModuleGrading, checking isHomogeneous on vectors/modules.

rubrics_metrics.name: isSublattice
rubrics_metrics.description: checks whether the lattice created by L is a sublattice of the lattice created by S
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Usage: isSublattice(L, S); L, S are intmat. Purpose: checks whether each generator of L is contained in S. Return: integer, 0 if false, 1 if true. Examples show cases returning 1 and a negative example using not(isSublattice(...)).

rubrics_metrics.name: imageLattice
rubrics_metrics.description: compute an integral basis for the image of the lattice L under the homomorphism of lattices Q
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Usage: imageLattice(Q,L); Q and L are intmat. Returns: intmat (basis for image lattice). Example: given Q (2x3) and L (3x2), documentation shows expected 2x2 result and prints actual output.

rubrics_metrics.name: intRank
rubrics_metrics.description: compute the rank of the integral matrix A by computing a hermite normalform
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Usage: intRank(A); A intmat. Returns: int. Examples: shows computing rank of matrices A and B and printed expected ranks; implemented via Hermite NF.

rubrics_metrics.name: kernelLattice
rubrics_metrics.description: compute an integral basis for the kernel of the homomorphism of lattices defined by the intmat P
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Usage: kernelLattice(P); P intmat. Returns: intmat (basis for kernel lattice). Examples: given LL (3x4) returns a 4x2 matrix whose columns generate kernel lattice; second example shown and printed.

rubrics_metrics.name: latticeBasis
rubrics_metrics.description: compute an integral basis for the lattice defined by the columns of B
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Usage: latticeBasis(B); B intmat. Returns: intmat basis whose columns generate same lattice as input. Examples: shows L (3x3) and result; second example with C (2x4) demonstrates expected canonical basis.

rubrics_metrics.name: preimageLattice
rubrics_metrics.description: compute an integral basis for the preimage of B under the homomorphism of lattices defined by the intmat P
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Usage: preimageLattice(P, B); P, B are intmat. Returns: intmat. Examples: show expected preimage basis columns for sample P and B; prints preimage results.

rubrics_metrics.name: projectLattice
rubrics_metrics.description: Given columns of B (vectors in ZZ^m), provide a linear map ZZ^m -> ZZ^n having the primitive span of B as its kernel
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Usage: projectLattice(B); B intmat. Returns: intmat (map matrix). Examples: several sample Bs and expected projectLattice outputs shown; output matrices correspond to kernels generated by described vectors.

rubrics_metrics.name: intersectLattices
rubrics_metrics.description: compute an integral basis for the intersection of the lattices A and B
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Usage: intersectLattices(A, B); A, B intmat. Returns: intmat basis for intersection. Examples: two examples provided showing expected columns for the intersection lattices and printed results.

rubrics_metrics.name: isIntegralSurjective
rubrics_metrics.description: test whether the given linear map P of lattices is surjective
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Purpose/Return: int, where 0 is false and 1 is true. Examples: intmat A (2x3) yields 0; another example B yields 1. Use print(b) to see result.

rubrics_metrics.name: isPrimitiveSublattice
rubrics_metrics.description: check whether the given set of integral vectors (columns of A) generate a primitive sublattice in ZZ^m (a direct summand of ZZ^m)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Return: int, 0 false, 1 true. Examples: A (3x2) returns 0; B (2x2 identity) returns 1.

rubrics_metrics.name: intInverse
rubrics_metrics.description: compute the integral inverse of the intmat A. If det(A) is neither 1 nor -1 an error is returned.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Purpose/Return: intmat (integral inverse). Examples: intInverse(A) for unimodular A returns unit matrix when multiplied by A; for matrices with det != ±1 an error is expected.

rubrics_metrics.name: integralSection
rubrics_metrics.description: for a given linear surjective map P of lattices this procedure returns an integral section of P
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Usage: integralSection(P). Returns: intmat U such that P * U = identity on image. Example: prints U and verifies P * U, demonstrating returned columns form a section.

rubrics_metrics.name: primitiveSpan
rubrics_metrics.description: compute an integral basis for the minimal primitive sublattice that contains the given vectors (columns of V)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Usage: primitiveSpan(V). Returns: intmat whose columns generate the minimal primitive sublattice containing inputs. Examples show expected canonicalizations of input columns.

rubrics_metrics.name: factorgroup
rubrics_metrics.description: returns a representation of the factor group G mod H using the first isomorphism theorem
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Usage: factorgroup(G,H); list G, list H (groups). Returns: list representation of factor group. Example: build G and H with createGroup and call factorgroup(G,H) to get representation printed as list entries.

rubrics_metrics.name: productgroup
rubrics_metrics.description: Returns a representation of the group G x H
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Usage: productgroup(G,H); list G, list H. Returns: list (representation of product group). Example: creating groups and calling productgroup returns list with appropriate S and L matrices representing the product; printed output shows combined S and L blocks.

rubrics_metrics.name: multiDeg
rubrics_metrics.description: compute multidegree of a polynomial/vector/ideal/module
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Usage: multiDeg(A); A is polynomial/vector/ideal/module. Purpose: compute multidegree relative to current ring multigrading. Examples: with setBaseMultigrading various computations for monomials, polynomials, ideals, vectors, modules illustrated; multiDeg(0) returns 0 vector; multiDeg on modules/vectors uses module grading if present. Notes: examples show behavior with torsion, different base gradings, and usage of attrib to set gradingGroup.

rubrics_metrics.name: multiDegBasis
rubrics_metrics.description: compute all monomials of multidegree d (assumes current ring is multigraded, monomial ordering is global)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Usage: multiDegBasis(d), where d is intvec. Returns list of monomials of that multidegree. Examples: many examples illustrating different base gradings, torsion, and corner cases. Note doc mentions some BUG??? comments in examples when using qring; examples show attribute "ZeroPart" on returned list to indicate zero-part monomials.

rubrics_metrics.name: multiDegPartition
rubrics_metrics.description: Returns an ideal/module consisting of multigraded-homogeneous parts of p
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Usage: multiDegPartition(def p), with p a polynomial/vector/module. Returns partitioned homogeneous parts as ideal/module entries. Examples: partitioning polynomial f into homogeneous parts under setBaseMultigrading, and partitioning module vectors with setModuleGrading to separate homogeneous components.

rubrics_metrics.name: isTorsionFree
rubrics_metrics.description: Determines whether the multigrading attached to the current ring is free.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Usage: isTorsionFree(). Return: boolean (1 true, 0 false). Example: setBaseMultigrading with matrices M,T showing torsion-free case returns 1; different B shows non-free and returns 0.

rubrics_metrics.name: isPositive
rubrics_metrics.description: Computes whether the multigrading of the ring is positive. For computation theorem 8.6 of the Miller/Sturmfels book is used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Usage: isPositive(). Returns true if the multigrading is positive. Example: setBaseMultigrading(A) where A = [-1,1] returns 0 (not positive); B = [1,1] returns 1. printlevel can be set for debugging.

rubrics_metrics.name: isZeroElement
rubrics_metrics.description: For an integer vector 'd' representing the multidegree of some polynomial or vector this method computes if the multidegree is contained in the grading group (either set globally or given as an optional argument), i.e. if it is zero in the multigrading.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Usage: isZeroElement(d, [T]); d intvec, optional group T. Return: boolean (1 if zero element). Examples: compute differences of multiDegs and test with and without alternative torsion group tt to illustrate when a degree difference is zero in the group.

rubrics_metrics.name: areZeroElements
rubrics_metrics.description: For an integer matrix D (considered column-wise as set of integer vectors) this method checks whether all these multidegrees are contained in the grading group (either set globally or given as an optional argument), i.e. if they all are zero in the multigrading.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Usage: areZeroElements(D, [T]); D intmat, optional group T. Returns boolean. Examples demonstrate assembling multidegrees of polynomials/ideals into matrix m and testing areZeroElements(m) returning 1 or 0 depending on grading/group.

rubrics_metrics.name: isHomogeneous
rubrics_metrics.description: Return TRUE if a is (multi)homogeneous, and FALSE otherwise
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Usage: isHomogeneous(a[, f]); a polynomial/vector/ideal/module. Return: boolean. Examples: After setBaseMultigrading, isHomogeneous distinguishes polynomials that partition into multiple multidegree parts; there is a 'checkGens' option in examples that checks generator-wise homogeneity (example shows difference). Also note: setModuleGrading must be consistent; multiple examples illustrate checking modules, vectors, and module generators for homogeneity and using multiDegPartition.

rubrics_metrics.name: equalMultiDeg
rubrics_metrics.description: Tests if the exponent vectors of two monomials (given by exp1 and exp2) represent the same multidegree.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Usage: equalMultiDeg(exp1, exp2[, V]); exp1, exp2 intvec, optional V intmat encodes module component multidegrees. Return: int (1 if equal). Examples: many pairwise comparisons of leadexp(...) for monomials a,b,c,d,e,f under setBaseMultigrading show which exponent vectors represent the same multidegree.

rubrics_metrics.name: multiDegGroebner
rubrics_metrics.description: computes the multigraded standard/groebner basis of I
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Usage: multiDegGroebner(I); I is poly/vector/ideal/module. Purpose: computes multigraded Groebner/standard basis. Note: I must be multigraded homogeneous. Returns ideal/module (the computed basis). Examples: setBaseMultigrading, setModuleGrading for module M then call M = multiDegGroebner(M) producing basis; further example computes multidegree syzygies via multiDegSyzygy(M) and then runs multiDegGroebner on S.
